intro.title: Descendant and child selectors
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple family tree webpage to practice selecting nested HTML elements. You will learn the core CSS concepts of descendant selectors (which target elements anywhere inside an ancestor) and child selectors (which target only direct children). The main technologies involved are CSS selectors, using spaces for descendants and the '>' symbol for children. By the end, you'll be able to style specific parts of a nested structure with precision.
intro.usecase: Descendant and child selectors are essential for styling nested UI components in real-world applications. For example, in a dashboard with multiple panels, you can use descendant selectors to style all paragraphs within a specific panel, while child selectors ensure only direct list items in a navigation menu receive a particular style. This allows developers to create clean, maintainable CSS for complex layouts like e-commerce product grids, admin settings forms, or social media feeds without affecting unintended elements.
